newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end lower as blue chips lose momentum.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end lower as blue chips lose momentum.

text.p: Swiss shares failed to maintain an early upward drive, snapping a four-day bull run to end lower as bourse heavyweights such as Novartis, UBS and Nestle turned negative on early Wall Street losses.
The market focused on insurer Winterthur, whose extreme volatility was representative of the whole market, dealers said.
* Winterthur shares took centre stage. The shares gave up most of their eight percent gain to end 16 francs higher at 1,420 after the company said its share price was excessive.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) down 35.5 points, or 0.59 percent, to 5,977.1.
The SMI had touched an all-time high at 6,101.2 points in early trade, powering ahead after breaching the psychologically important level of 6,000 points on Tuesday.
* The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 15.62 points, or 0.41 percent, to 3,753.17.
Bourse volume reached a hefty 3.69 billion Swiss francs.
Unconfirmed rumours have circulated in the market that Winterthur may reinforce its ties with bank group CS Group, but dealers said this speculation was old.
A Winterthur spokeswoman said the firm did not plan any kind of substantial changes.
* Credit Suisse Group lost two francs to 207.25. UBS bearers slid 11 francs to 1,729.

* Shares of technology group Sulzer were among the star performers. Dealers said this stemmed from the fact that its Sulzer Medica unit said sales in the first six months of 1997 rose 22 percent to 704 million Swiss francs.
Sulzer Medica is in the process of being partially spun off. Trade in Sulzer Medica will start next week.
* Novartis registereds fell 26 francs to 2,453 but Roche certificates rose 65 francs to 14,650.
* On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), trade was hectic in late trade as the cash market was shaken by early Wall Street losses.
Dealers said SMI futures came under pressure in late trade. SMI July futures were down 38.5 points to stand at 5,979.0 points. Total volume in SMI futures reached 6,249 contracts.
On the options side, 177,350 contracts changed hands. The call/put ratio was at 1.33 to one.
